title: Commission a recirculating water-heater PI loop
principalTechnique: Model-qualified PI structure and tuning decision
objective: Derive, identify, validate, tune, and abnormally qualify one unapplied PI recommendation for a continuously modulated recirculating water heater.
physicalPurpose: Maintain outlet-water temperature through setpoint and cold-water-load changes while respecting one-sided heater authority, limits, manual operation, and evidence boundaries.

simplifications: The recirculating water volume is represented by one well-mixed FOPDT temperature state.
The power stage has ideal amplitude limits and omits element temperature, boiling, electrical protection, circulation loss, and pump failure.
The physical derivation and identification record are exact deterministic teaching evidence, not measurements from installed equipment.
All controller and plant results are Simulation evidence and cannot authorize physical application.

baseline.limitation: P plus correct nominal bias retains changed-load offset, while the historical PI has not yet been justified against independently validated model and robustness evidence.

change.decision: Compare all four structures on equivalent nominal and uncertainty scenarios, preserve the confirmed revision, and export the simplest eligible PI as an unapplied recommendation.

disturbances: Lower each plant copy's zero-power equilibrium by 3 degC at 100 seconds.
Request the deliberately unreachable 45 degC setpoint from 140 through 170 seconds and restore 35 degC.
Use manual 60 percent heater power from 180 through 185 seconds and invalidate temperature quality from 190 through 192 seconds.
Repeat Robust and Balanced PI validation with process gain 0.16 and 0.24 degC/% and delay 1.5 seconds.

acceptance.window: 130 through 140 seconds after settling qualification for every declared uncertainty scenario

abortPredicates: Temperature, timing, model coefficient, requested power, or applied power is nonfinite or outside its declared range.
The identification experiment leaves its approved power, temperature, duration, circulation, or operating-region boundary.
A candidate is ranked from unvalidated model evidence or an unqualified response.
The confirmed controller revision changes without separate explicit application approval.
Simulation evidence is presented as physical commissioning or independent overtemperature protection.
safety.restorationMode: Track the reviewed manual heater power, restore valid measurement and circulation evidence, then explicitly return the unchanged confirmed controller to automatic mode.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer with electrical, mechanical, operations, water-quality and safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Do not energize a physical heater, change a physical controller, or bypass independent trips.
Physical identification requires reviewed circulation, temperature, power, duration, abort and rollback boundaries immediately before excitation.
Applying the exported recommendation requires separate explicit approval and a rollback-ready commissioning window.

video.viewerOutcome: Complete a defensible process-control commissioning decision from plant physics and data through an unapplied PI recommendation.

learning.context: A continuously modulated one-sided electric heater maintains 35 degC outlet water around a 75 percent operating point while cold-water load, noise, limits and mode changes act on the loop.
learning.reason: Separate lessons established P, bias, integral, PI, anti-windup, modelling, identification and tuning; the capstone requires one auditable choice rather than disconnected demonstrations.
theory: Thermal equilibrium predicts the nominal holding power from zero-power temperature, steady process gain and desired outlet temperature.
A physical model and an identified model have different evidence sources and both require independent validation before tuning authority.
PI is the simplest eligible structure when prompt correction and zero constant-load error are required; derivative action needs separate benefit and noise evidence.
Combined anti-windup acts on the controller's private nominal and bounded outputs, while public requested and applied power expose actuator behavior without inventing private state.
Robust and Balanced SIMC candidates trade error response, actuator movement and uncertainty reserve rather than supplying a universal winner.
learning.workedPrediction: Calculate 75 percent holding power and independently reproduce Robust gains 3.26087/0.65217 and Balanced gains 5.76923/1.15385 from the validated 0.2, 5 second, 1 second FOPDT model.
practicalPreparation: Declare requirements, model assumptions, identification approval, independent validation record, candidates, measures, uncertainty cases, limits, modes, aborts, rollback and Simulation label.
Predict P-plus-bias load offset and the Robust-versus-Balanced response/activity tradeoff before running.
learning.baseline: Validate P plus 75 percent bias and historical PI on equivalent copies, retaining both the P load offset and the historical PI's real performance.
learning.change: Calculate and run Robust and Balanced SIMC PI candidates without changing controller revision 77.
learning.comparison: Classify model, run and candidate eligibility before comparing final-window error, overshoot, IAE, applied-power total variation, saturation recovery and uncertainty results.
learning.validation: Repeat nominal, cold-load, sensor, unreachable-demand, restoration, manual, quality, gain-variation and delay-variation cases; retain the recommendation as unapplied.
learning.explanation: Connect energy balance, identified dynamics, structure choice, tuning calculations, actuator constraints, anti-windup, tracking and uncertainty evidence into one causal decision.
learning.transfer: Carry complete commissioning discipline into Lesson 78, where a servo adds derivative damping, resonance, frequency-domain evidence, discrete implementation, encoder noise and torque limits.
